precepts.text: He that loveth gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof. Gold hath been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present. Sometimes money is your ruin: you stop making sound decisions, you are willing to do anything for it. That is why you see these young women degrading themselves on these platforms for money; what morals do you have, and then you go home and kiss your kids? It is a stumblingblock unto them that sacrifice unto it. If money is all you think about and all you talk about, if your existence is based off money, then that is your god; you made a sacrifice to it. But blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and hath not gone after gold. Why? Because it is hard to have riches and keep the commandments; with money you can be enticed so many ways, because you can do whatever you want. But when you are without blemish, you use those finances properly and it does not mess with your head. You have a lot of money, but you have not made it your god.
precepts.point: This man walked with Christ. He saw the healing, he was around the commandment keeping; but that money lust is never enough. He desired money and riches more than anything. And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver. And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him. Ultimately Judas betrayed Lord Jesus Christ.
precepts.why:
Judas asked the chief priests, “What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you?” and “they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.” Sirach shows what that love of money does: “He that loveth gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.”

“Gold hath been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.” Sometimes money is the ruin of you. You stop making sound decisions; you are willing to do anything for it. That is why so many young women today are on OnlyFans and on these podcasts, doing anything they can to make money, willing to get booed on in another country for money. What morals do you have, and then you go home and kiss your kids? It might look good because of the opportunity, but all things ain't good.

“It is a stumblingblock unto them that sacrifice unto it, and every fool shall be taken therewith.” If money is all you think about and all you talk about, if your existence is based off money, money, money, then that is your god. That is why it says you made a sacrifice to it.

“Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and hath not gone after gold.” Why blessed? Because it is hard to have riches and keep the commandments. With money you can be enticed in so many ways; you can buy what you want and do whatever you want, and some feel they are above everybody. But when you are without blemish, you use your finances properly and it don't mess with your head. You have a lot of money, but you ain't made it your god.

Judas walked with Christ. He saw the healing and was around the commandment keeping, but that money lust is never enough, and he desired riches more than anything. Gold was his ruin: money was his demise.

precepts.text: Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart and cheerfulness of the mind; but wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind. The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element the Lord created has its function and purpose, but if you abuse it you cannot be useful to the nation. It goes for food as well; that is why they put the fast food across the street from more fast food in our neighborhoods. They are depending on you to fall into that destruction.
precepts.point: Captain's teaching: it is not a sin to drink, but when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good, which is God's laws.

note.label: The Developmental Psychology of Being Hated

precepts.why:
“Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind”. Measurably. The wine is not the sin; the measure is the key. “But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind”. That is the key point: bitterness of the mind.

The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element on the earth was created by the Lord, and it has its function and its purpose. But if you use it and abuse it, you cannot be useful for the nation.

It is the same with alcoholism as it is with food, which the Bishop has been bringing out: all of it has a balance, and if you overuse it you fall. Our oppressors are depending on us to lose that balance. That is why you have the KFCs across the street from Domino's, and the liquor stores in our neighborhoods: they are depending on you to fall into that destruction, that chaos, that confusion.

Nobody out there is drinking measurably or sociably; it is used to drown out reality, and it will kill you. So overcoming evil with good means holding the balance the Most High set in every element, and not letting the bottle become the outlet.

precepts.text: Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing, and what is created more wicked than an eye? Therefore it weepeth upon every occasion. It starts with the desire of what you see, then the mind decides whether to feed the lust.
precepts.point: The brain stores everything: a random song from years ago surfaces because it is saved in long-term memory, the way your stuff never really leaves the internet. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and often we do not realize we are being controlled; you were made in a factory called America and those are not your words. The only way to break the code is to reprogram and recode.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked than an eye? therefore it weepeth upon every occasion.” The eye is where it starts. It starts with the desire of what you see, and then the mind decides whether to feed the lust.

That is why it belongs with Matthew 15. The Pharisees were arguing about eating with unwashed hands, and Christ told them that what goes in at the mouth goes into the belly and “is cast out into the draught”, but “those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.” What comes out of your mouth is the output value of what was put into your mind, and the eye is one of the ways it gets put in.

The brain stores everything you let in. A random song or thought from years ago comes out of you because it was saved in long-term memory, the same way your stuff on the internet never really leaves. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and a lot of times we don't even realize we are being controlled. You were made in a factory called America, and those are not your words. The only way to break that code is to reprogram and recode, and the wicked eye is where the guarding has to begin.

precepts.text: Be quick in all thy works, including how you eat, so shall there no sickness come unto thee.
precepts.point: The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
“My son, hear me, and despise me not, and at the last thou shalt find as I told thee: in all thy works be quick, so shall there no sickness come unto thee.” Be quick in all thy works, and that includes how you eat.

The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live. Caleb's strength at eighty-five was the same as in the day Moses sent him; that is the health the Most High keeps for those who are quick.

precepts.text: Wine drunk moderately is as good as life and makes men glad, but with excess it brings bitterness.
precepts.point: Wine makes glad the heart of man and oil makes his face to shine. This shows we are dark-skinned people, for oil is put on dry skin to make it shine, and the scriptures describe us.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man’s heart.” Wine makes glad the heart of man, and Ecclesiasticus says how: “Wine is as good as life to a man, if it be drunk moderately: what life is then to a man that is without wine? for it was made to make men glad.”

Wine drunk moderately is as good as life and was made to make men glad. “Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind: But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind, with brawling and quarrelling.” Measurably and in season it brings gladness of the heart; with excess it brings bitterness, brawling and quarrelling.

So the wine that makes glad the heart of man is wine drunk in measure. The Most High brought it out of the earth for gladness, not for excess.
